title: Same day, four filters
prompt: Finance's daily takings report picks the trips that started on 7 April 2026. Four drafts pick that day in different ways. Before anyone times them, write `solve(trips)` so it reports, for each draft, whether it returns the same rows as `as_text`, how many rows it returns and how many rows its file scan handed on.
rules: One row per draft in `VERSIONS`: `version` (its name), `same_rows`, `rows`, `scan_rows`. Don't change the drafts.
`same_rows` is true when the draft returns exactly the rows `as_text` returns, duplicates included; `as_text` matches itself.
`rows` counts the rows the draft returns; `scan_rows` is what the `Scan csv` step handed on in one run.
hints: Two drafts can return the same number of rows and still differ. Compare the sorted rows from `collect()`.
Build each draft fresh for its profile, then pick the step whose name is `Scan csv` (names in `profile` are indented).
A condition the CSV reader understands is applied as it reads, so its scan hands on fewer rows. Text built from the timestamp isn't one of them.
explanation: Check the rows first: for each draft, compare `sorted(build(trips).collect())` with the same for `as_text`. `as_date` and `time_range` return the same trips. `after_midnight` returns as many rows on the sample but not the same ones: it drops the trip at exactly midnight on the 7th and adds the one at midnight on the 8th, so it's a bug, however fast it is. Then profile a fresh copy of each draft and read the `Scan csv` step. `as_text` turns the timestamp into text, which the CSV reader can't test while reading, so its scan hands on every trip and the `Filter` step does the work. The others are pushed into the reader, and so is `as_date`: Catalyst rewrites a cast to date into a time range. All four read the whole file either way; the profile says which ones hand fewer rows to the next step, not how long that takes.
